why: UNIVERSES: all 115 theorems of the item are taken at universe 0 (the examples have none). A_to_B uses five conjuncts. One_homeo_cls gives a homeomorphism whose underlying map is GenSBMap.orbitOrMap, which is (1a). Theorem_12_5_7_cls gives fibre preservation over smoothOrbitMap, which is (1b), and that the induced map is D.orbitOrMap for every representative; with D = SDiagram.id this plus the non-item SDiagram.orbitOrMap_id is the identity part of (1c). Theorem_12_5_7_functorial is the composition part of (1c). For (2), two_cls gives o' (continuous, invariant) related to o through orEqv on the representative W ← V → W'. Then orbitOrMap_mk, smoothOrbitMap_bijective for Φ, and the invariance of o and o' along morphisms turn that relation into B's: |f̄|_*|(a,o_a)| = |(a',o'_{a'})| whenever |f|(|a|) = |a'|. B_to_A is not proved because most of A is more general than B or is extra content. That includes the local-orientation (Loc) versions (no bump functions and no sc⁺-sections through fibre points), the class-level statements without any topology, and the statements for a single strong bundle equivalence. It also includes representative independence under |f| = |g| with the IsLRLocal hypothesis, the rep_indep/refinement/naturality lemmas, the non-effective example (two different classes inducing the same map) and the concrete witnesses. B_to_A_functorial derives the functoriality conjunct from B (1c). The other conjuncts would need the orientation-transfer theory of §12.5 to be re-proved.
overlap: HARNESS: the item's statements carry banned theorems as proof arguments inside their types. GenSBMap.orbitOrMap is Equiv.ofBijective _ (orbitOrMap_bijective …), the pulled-back bundle uses IsStrongBundleEquivalence.hasScPlusSectionsThrough, orEqv uses orEqv_apply/orMor_orEqv, SDiagram.comp uses equivalences_compRight, and the Loc statements use orLoc_square, isTame_B, transferT/K_mpullPt₃ and others. So plain #rt_check and #rt_check_soft both fail on A_to_B and B_to_A_functorial; the failures are recorded with #guard_msgs. The file also checks the bare statements (stmtA := A, stmtB := B, stmtF := the functoriality statement). The 14 banned names reached by A_to_B are exactly those reached by stmtA ∪ stmtB, and the 6 reached by B_to_A_functorial lie in stmtB ∪ stmtF. So no banned theorem enters through a proof step. The proofs cite only A's conjuncts (as hypotheses) and the non-item lemmas GenSBMap.rep/cls_rep, isEquivalence_rep_Ψ, sbe, smoothRel_of_quot_eq, SDiagram.orbitOrMap_id and eq_pushforward_comp. GenSBMap.theorem_12_5_7_id was deliberately not used, since its proof goes through the banned orbitOrMap_eq_of_equiv. rt_overlap B_to_A_functorial: 5638 shared project theorems, essentially all from the statements (the Part I orientation machinery under orTopology and the strong-bundle localization).
